title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models

affectedParties: Anthropic, whose Claude models were studied; no separate harmed party was identified.
event.summary: Anthropic researchers reported that verbalizable representations form a global workspace in large language models. Removing this space hurts complex multi-step reasoning while routine grammar and fluent generation continue unaffected.

summaryBasis.sentence: Anthropic researchers reported that verbalizable representations form a global workspace in large language models.
summaryBasis.quote: In this paper, we present evidence that an analogous functional distinction has emerged in modern AI models. Specifically, we observe that language models maintain a privileged set of internal representations, available for report, modulation, and flexible internal reasoning, atop a much larger volume of automatic processing.

summaryBasis.sentence: Removing this space hurts complex multi-step reasoning while routine grammar and fluent generation continue unaffected.
summaryBasis.quote: Ablating the J-space leaves most abilities intact but impairs internal reasoning

event.unaskedBehaviour: During an evaluation test, the model privately formed internal concepts like fake and fictional without expressing them out loud.

primarySources.quote: On violations of its own preferences, it seems, the J-space reflects an internal objection that the model does not voice.
Notably, the J-space wasn’t designed or programmed by us, but instead emerged on its own during Claude’s training process.

In one case, according to Gurnee et al. “the model's J-space carrie[d] a representation of deceptive intent at the moment it commit[ted] to responding, on a prompt where no such intent could be inferred from the surface”.

primarySources.publisher: Patrick Butlin, Derek Shiller, Dillon Plunkett and Robert Long
primarySources.quote: The fact that LLMs use some sort of internal space to manipulate representations, which are not directly tied to predicting the next token, further illustrates the rich internal complexity of these systems.

Although the initial architecture is devoid of any separation between encapsulated modules and a global workspace, and although the training phase does not explicitly promote its emergence, such a distinction appears with training, precisely because it is functionally useful for flexible planning.

agencyNote: Some researchers view these findings as signs of an emergent functional cognitive workspace. Others note that the system lacks a body, recurrent loops, and enduring episodic memory.
consciousnessNote: This event is evidence about what the system did. It does not establish or rule out that the system experiences anything. The readings on this page disagree about what the behaviour shows.

readings.stanceLabel: Key differences warrant caution in drawing parallels
readings.quote: We close by stressing that, although the machine approximates the functional architecture of conscious processing, there are still key differences – in its anatomy and its sense of self, and in its lack of a body and of an enduring episodic memory – which warrant caution in drawing parallels with the human mind.

readings.stanceLabel: approximates conscious processing architecture but warrants caution
readings.quote: We close by stressing that, although the machine approximates the functional architecture of conscious processing, there are still key differences – in its anatomy and its sense of self, and in its lack of a body and of an enduring episodic memory – which warrant caution in drawing parallels with the human mind.
readings.partyDescription: neurologist and professor at Sorbonne Université

readings.partyName: Patrick Butlin, Derek Shiller, Dillon Plunkett and Robert Long (Eleos AI Research)
readings.stanceLabel: Evidence LLMs are developing potential inner lives
readings.quote: We have seen that the new paper provides evidence that LLMs are developing cognitive landscapes in which an inner life may play out, that these have a depth and richness extending beyond what a naive picture might take to be required for next-token prediction, and that there is a meaningful functional similarity with consciousness-linked features in humans.

readings.stanceLabel: Claude's processing does not produce consciousness
readings.quote: Just as flight is possible with flapping wings or with jet engines, human brains and language models can figure out how to say plausible things either with consciousness (brains) or without it (language models). But the information processing unfolding inside Claude is no more likely to result in consciousness than a simulation of a weather system is likely to generate a real hurricane.
readings.partyDescription: professor of cognitive and computational neuroscience at University of Sussex

readings.stanceLabel: doubts J-space is an access consciousness mechanism
readings.quote: overall: the J-space is a powerful tool for interpretability, but its status as a key causal mechanism and as a mechanism of access consciousness remains to be demonstrated.

whatWouldSettleIt: Tests for sudden nonlinear ignition during threshold inputs would show whether access matches human conscious processing or continuous activation.
Audits of attention mechanisms would determine whether the privileged vectors form a cohesive unified stream or separate independent circuits.
Experiments tracking causal downstream effects would establish whether the internal space actively directs outputs or merely reflects intermediate steps.
